question: In the combined dataset that unifies the trees data with the income data by ZIP code, filling missing ZIP values where necessary, which three boroughs, restricted to records with median and mean income both greater than zero and a valid borough name, contain the highest number of trees, and what is the average mean income for each of these three boroughs?
sql:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(t.zipcode, i.zipcode) as zipcode,
    t.boroname,
    t.tree_id,
    i.Estimate_Median_income,
    i.Estimate_Mean_income
  FROM trees t
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT zipcode, Estimate_Median_income, Estimate_Mean_income
    FROM income_trees
  ) i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM combined
  WHERE Estimate_Median_income > 0 
    AND Estimate_Mean_income > 0 
    AND boroname IS NOT NULL
    AND boroname != ''
)
SELECT boroname, ROUND(AVG(Estimate_Mean_income), 2) as avg_mean_income
FROM filtered
WHERE tree_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY boroname
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 3

WITH combined AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(t.zipcode, i.zipcode) as zipcode,
    t.boroname,
    t.tree_id,
    i.Estimate_Median_income,
    i.Estimate_Mean_income
  FROM trees t
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT zipcode, Estimate_Median_income, Estimate_Mean_income
    FROM income_trees
  ) i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM combined
  WHERE Estimate_Median_income > 0 
    AND Estimate_Mean_income > 0 
    AND boroname IS NOT NULL
    AND boroname != ''
)
SELECT boroname, COUNT(*) as tree_count, ROUND(AVG(Estimate_Mean_income), 2) as avg_mean_income
FROM filtered
WHERE tree_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY boroname
ORDER BY tree_count DESC
